catalog_quote: Words in Southern Katang are both monosyllabic and disyllabic. [...] In terms of disyllabic words, there are two elements: a presyllable and a main syllable. The maximal syllable structure is /c1{v1/c2}. C3(C4)V2(C5)/. It should be noted that the term presyllable goes by different names, such as minor syllable, half syllable, consonantal prefix, and weak syllable. [...] The main syllable has the same structure as a monosyllabic word. Meanwhile, the presyllable is different. [...] there is no contrastive presyllable vowel quality found in Southern Katang. The presyllable vowel is realized as a mid to open central vowel. [...] Based on this, the Southern Katang phonological word is a maximally disyllabic iamb (Gehrmann, 2018).

new_statements.rule_in_words: The phonological word is at most two syllables and iambic: a reduced, phonotactically restricted presyllable (vowel quality neutralised) followed by the prominent main (final) syllable; monosyllables are bare main syllables. I.e. word prominence is fixed on the final (main) syllable. The thesis states this as a word-template ('iamb') rather than with the word 'stress'; the explicit wording it relies on is Gehrmann 2018 p. 133 (main syllable 'always prosodically prominent', presyllable 'always unstressed', for the Katuic template that S. Katang is said to instantiate) and Gehrmann 2016 p. 76 ('Minor syllables, due to their unstressed position in the canonical WK word', West Katuic incl. Katang Rueal).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (words are maximally disyllabic, so no secondary stress arises).
new_statements.exceptions: None for prominence. Structural notes only: stop+liquid sequences are unpredictably either a cluster onset (/pluh/ 'blow') or presyllable+main syllable (/pa.luh/ 'meet'); /ʔN-/ presyllables have a syllabic nasal with no epenthetic vowel; presyllable rime is either a neutral vowel or a sonorant /l r N/.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word in citation form (1500-item wordlists from Huffman 1979 and Gehrmann 2013-15 recordings); no phrase-level prosody discussed. Register (not tone) is the other suprasegmental; the language is described as post-registral (register cued by vowel quality).
new_statements.identity_note: Yotmanisakun 2022 describes exactly Southern Katang [sct] = sout3251 (autonym Katang / Katang Rueal), from two speakers: Huffman's 1979 informant from Tesseng Nadu, Tumlan district, and Gehrmann's 2013-15 informant from Salavan district, Salavan province. Gehrmann 2016's 'KatR / Katang Rueal / Katang Salavan' is the same variety; his 'KatP / Katang Phin' is Northern Katang [ncq], a different language. 'Katang Ta'oiq' of Ta'oi district is an Upper Ta'oih [tth] dialect per the ISO 2016-021 request, not this language.

sources.note: Sec. 3.1 pp. 13-14 (and 4.2.1 pp. 46-47): words are maximally disyllabic (presyllable + main syllable); presyllable (a.k.a. 'weak syllable') has no vowel-quality contrast (realised mid-open central, written /a/); 'the Southern Katang phonological word is a maximally disyllabic iamb (Gehrmann, 2018)'. No section on stress as such; no stress marks in the 1500-item wordlist.

sources.citation: Gehrmann, Ryan. 2018. Katuic presyllables and derivational morphology in diachronic perspective. In H. Ring & F. Rau (eds.), Papers from ICAAL 7 (JSEALS Special Publication 3), 132-156. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. hdl:10524/52438
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 133: Katuic languages have 'prosodic words of a maximally disyllabic, iambic template'; the final/main syllable 'is always prosodically prominent' and the presyllable 'is always unstressed' (stated for the PK word template continued by the modern languages). Table 5 p. 136 lists S. Katang explicitly (Marginal Presyllables: no presyllable vowel contrast, contrastive sesquisyllabicity retained).

sources.citation: Gehrmann, Ryan. 2016. The West Katuic Languages: Comparative Phonology and Diagnostic Tools. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. 372 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Katang Rueal (KatR, Salavan district = Southern Katang) is one of his first-hand West Katuic varieties. Sec. 4.3 p. 76: 'Minor syllables, due to their unstressed position in the canonical WK word, are quite susceptible to diachronic sound change' (West-Katuic-general). Sec. 2.4.1.4 pp. 26-28 'Katang Salavan phonology' covers only vowels/register (Huffman's data).
